newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy prelim CPI seen at 3.4. pct yr/yr in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Italy prelim CPI seen at 3.4. pct yr/yr in Sept.

text.p: Italian consumer prices are seen at 3.4 percent year-on-year in September and 0.3 percent month on month after data issued by 10 sample cities, analysts said.
They confirmed forecasts made on Monday after the first six Italian cities announced their data.
On Tuesday, figures were given by Genoa, Florence, Naples and Palermo.
In August, final Italian CPI stood at 3.4 percent year-on-year and rose 0.1 percent on a month-on-month basis.
Final national inflation data for September will be issued by statistics institute ISTAT on October 4.

"Tonight's data were decisively better than last night's," an analyst at Banque Indosuez in Milan said. "They don't change expectations of a fall in official interest rates which could come at the end of October or beginning of November."
Indosuez forecast October annual inflation falling to 3.2 percent.
Angela Ancona of Banca Commerciale Italiana said that with the four cities' data tonight, she saw September annual inflation of 3.4 percent and a monthly 0.3 percent rise.

"The influence of rising football match tickets, like with Bologna and Perugia, doesn't come into it. Genoa and Florence data, where prices were unchanged or lower month-on-month, show that the slowdown in inflation is continuing," she added.
Bruno Rovelli of Bank of America Milan agreed, "They are much better because the soccer match prices don't apply."
Deutsche Bank research office said it also forecast a September annual CPI rate of 3.4 percent and month-on-month rise of 0.3 percent.

"Net of exceptional factors, the trend is still good. If data from other cities outside the 10 sample ones - accounting for some 30 percent of the national weighting - confirm the positive trend we might even see a September rate of 3.3 percent - difficult but not to be excluded," Deutsche Bank said. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
